title: Telling what happened
job: A four-sentence account in the past
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: ASPECT AT LENGTH, and this is where L1's pairs finally get their rule. The perfective presents an action as a COMPLETED WHOLE with a result and moves the account forward a step; the imperfective presents it as a process, a repetition, or simply names the activity, and it paints the standing situation. Ya prochitál gazétu i poshyól domóy against Ya chitál gazétu, kogdá on pozvoníl.

THE SLOGAN TO KILL: "perfective is completed, imperfective is ongoing". It breaks on the first real account. Ya dva chasá chitál is bounded and imperfective; Ya prochitál za dva chasá is perfective; the reading took the same two hours. What differs is how the clause is being USED in the telling — as a whole with a result, or as background and process. Duration does not decide it, and neither does repetition.

One fact makes aspect visible, and the learner already has it: THE PERFECTIVE HAS NO PRESENT TENSE. L1-M6's napishú, pozvonyú and kuplyú are futures for exactly that reason. Use it as a test rather than memorising pairs — if a form has no present, it is perfective.

The sequencers are the honest new spend: snachála, kogdá, v kontsé, poslé étovo, joining L1-M10's potóm, i, a and no. Everything else in these accounts is recombination, and each account is four short sentences rather than one long one.

Nothing new is opened. Reflexive verbs stay out as a system — L1-M9's nrávitsya and this module's vernúlsya ride as vocabulary and the -sya rule is L3's — and so do the conditional by, participles, and prefixed motion verbs beyond L1's po- and pri-.

sentences.display: Snachála ya výpil chay. Potóm ya poshyól na rabótu
sentences.script: Сначала я выпил чай. Потом я пошёл на работу
sentences.cue: First I drank tea. Then I went to work
sentences.literal: At-first I drank-up tea. Then I went to work

words.note: Opens an account. It is one word built from "from the beginning", and it pairs with potóm as naturally as English's first pairs with then.

sentences.trap: výpil is perfective — the tea got drunk and the account moves on. L1-M5 shipped it beside p'yu without saying why the two look unrelated; this is why.
sentences.sound: sna-CHA-la ya VY-pil chay. The vy- prefix takes the stress off the stem, which is what perfective prefixes usually do.

variations.display: Snachála ya výpil chay. Potóm ya poshyól domóy
variations.script: Сначала я выпил чай. Потом я пошёл домой
variations.cue: First I drank tea. Then I went home
variations.changed: a different destination

variations.cue: First she drank tea
variations.changed: a woman, so the past agrees with her

variations.display: Ya výpil chay i poshyól na rabótu
variations.script: Я выпил чай и пошёл на работу
variations.cue: I drank tea and went to work
variations.changed: joined with i instead of split in two

mistake.display: Snachála ya pil chay. Potóm ya poshyól na rabótu
mistake.script: Сначала я пил чай. Потом я пошёл на работу
mistake.why: A step in an account is perfective: Snachála ya výpil chay.

sentences.usage: Telling someone how the morning went.

sentences.display: Ya chitál gazétu, kogdá on pozvoníl
sentences.script: Я читал газету, когда он позвонил
sentences.cue: I was reading the paper when he called
sentences.literal: I was-reading paper, when he called

words.note: It glues the two aspects together: the background before it, the event after it. It also asks a question — Kogdá vy prishlí? — and the word is the same.
L1-M3's chitát' in the past. Imperfective, so it paints the standing situation rather than moving the account — its partner prochitál is what finishes the paper.

sentences.trap: Both halves are past and neither is more past than the other. The imperfective is the background and the perfective the event, and that is a choice about the telling rather than about the clock.
sentences.sound: ya chi-TAL ga-ZYE-tu kag-DA on paz-va-NIL. Every verb in the line is stressed on its last syllable.

variations.display: Ya chitála gazétu, kogdá on pozvoníl
variations.script: Я читала газету, когда он позвонил
variations.cue: I was reading the paper when he called
variations.changed: said by a woman

variations.cue: I was working when she called
variations.changed: a different background and a different caller

variations.display: Ya prochitál gazétu i poshyól domóy
variations.script: Я прочитал газету и пошёл домой
variations.cue: I read the paper and went home
variations.changed: both perfective — two steps, no background

mistake.display: Ya prochitál gazétu, kogdá on pozvoníl
mistake.script: Я прочитал газету, когда он позвонил
mistake.why: The background clause is imperfective: Ya chitál gazétu, kogdá on pozvoníl.

sentences.usage: Explaining what you were in the middle of.

sentences.display: Ya dva chasá chitál. Potóm ya prochitál knígu
sentences.script: Я два часа читал. Потом я прочитал книгу
sentences.cue: I read for two hours. Then I finished the book
sentences.literal: I two hours was-reading. Then I read-through book

words.note: chitál's partner, and its own row — aspect partners never share one. The pro- says the reading reached its end, which is the result the account needs.

sentences.trap: The first clause has a duration in it and is IMPERFECTIVE anyway. "Ongoing" is not what the imperfective means — two hours is as bounded as anything gets, and the clause is still about the process.
sentences.sound: ya dva cha-SA chi-TAL. pa-TOM ya pra-chi-TAL KNI-gu. The two forms of the verb differ only in the prefix and where the stress sits.

variations.cue: I worked for two hours
variations.changed: a different activity, the same bounded imperfective

variations.display: Ya prochitál knígu za dva chasá
variations.script: Я прочитал книгу за два часа
variations.cue: I read the book in two hours
variations.changed: perfective, with the same two hours in it

variations.cue: She read for two hours
variations.changed: a woman as the subject

mistake.why: A stretch of time takes the imperfective: Ya dva chasá chitál.

sentences.usage: Saying how long something took, and then that it got finished.

sentences.display: Vcherá býlo khólodno, poéhtomu ya ostálsya dóma
sentences.script: Вчера было холодно, поэтому я остался дома
sentences.cue: Yesterday it was cold, so I stayed at home
sentences.literal: Yesterday was cold, therefore I stayed home

words.note: Another -sya verb arriving as vocabulary. The reflexive system is L3's; here it is simply the word for staying put.

sentences.trap: Býlo khólodno has no subject at all — it is the same shape as M1's Mne núzhno, and the past of it is just býlo. The weather is the fourth thing in this course with no subject.
sentences.sound: vchi-RA BY-la KHO-lad-na pa-EH-ta-mu ya as-TAL-sya DO-ma. Three unstressed o's reduce to a in poéhtomu alone.

variations.display: Vcherá býlo zhárko, poéhtomu ya ostálsya dóma
variations.script: Вчера было жарко, поэтому я остался дома
variations.cue: Yesterday it was hot, so I stayed at home
variations.changed: the other extreme

variations.display: Býlo khólodno, poéhtomu oná ostálas' dóma
variations.script: Было холодно, поэтому она осталась дома
variations.cue: It was cold, so she stayed at home
variations.changed: a woman, and the -sya becomes -s'

variations.cue: Yesterday it was cold
variations.changed: the first half alone

mistake.display: Vcherá byl khólodno, poéhtomu ya ostálsya dóma
mistake.script: Вчера был холодно, поэтому я остался дома
mistake.why: A subjectless past takes the neuter: Vcherá býlo khólodno.

sentences.usage: Explaining why a plan did not happen.
sentences.mnemonic: No subject means the neuter past.

sentences.display: Ya uvídel Ivána v magazíne. My poshlí v kafé
sentences.script: Я увидел Ивана в магазине. Мы пошли в кафе
sentences.cue: I saw Ivan in the shop. We went to a café
sentences.literal: I caught-sight Ivan in shop. We went into café

words.cue: caught sight of (said by a man)
words.note: The perfective of seeing: the moment of noticing. L1-M5's saw is its imperfective partner and names the activity of looking at something.
Indeclinable, like M4's metró and kinó. Borrowed words ending in a stressed vowel behave this way as a class.
One syllable, so no stress mark. L1 built we-are and we-will from other words and never opened the pronoun itself; an account needs it.

sentences.trap: uvídel is a moment and saw is a stretch. Both are "saw" in English, and only the aspect says which kind of seeing happened.
sentences.sound: ya u-VI-dil i-VA-na v ma-ga-ZI-nye. my pash-LI v ka-FE. The stress of kafé is on the last syllable and the word never moves.

variations.cue: I saw Ivan in the shop
variations.changed: said by a woman

variations.cue: We went to a café
variations.changed: the second half alone

variations.cue: I saw Anna in the street
variations.changed: a different person and place

mistake.why: An animate masculine name takes its accusative: Ya uvídel Ivána.

sentences.usage: The chance meeting, which is how half of all accounts start.
sentences.mnemonic: A moment of seeing is perfective.

words.note: The perfective past of M1's skazhíte. Its imperfective partner govoríl means "was saying" or "used to say", and is a different row.

sentences.trap: The clause after chto keeps the tense it was SPOKEN in. He said "vsyó khoroshó", so the report says vsyó khoroshó — Russian does not shift the tense back the way English does. The full reported-speech system is L3's; this much is safe because nothing shifts.
sentences.sound: on ska-ZAL shto vsyo kha-ra-SHO. chto is shto, and vsyo is one syllable with a yó in it.

variations.cue: She said everything was fine
variations.changed: a woman as the subject

variations.cue: He said he was at home
variations.changed: a present tense inside the report, unshifted

variations.cue: She said she was tired
variations.changed: L1-M2's short-form adjective inside the report

mistake.display: On skazál, chto vsyó bylo khoroshó
mistake.script: Он сказал, что всё было хорошо
mistake.why: Russian keeps the tense that was spoken: On skazál, chto vsyó khoroshó.

sentences.usage: Passing on what someone told you.
sentences.mnemonic: Russian does not shift the tense back.

sentences.display: Snachála my rabótali. Poslé étovo my poshlí domóy
sentences.script: Сначала мы работали. После этого мы пошли домой
sentences.cue: First we worked. After that we went home
sentences.literal: At-first we worked. After this we went home

words.note: A whole surface. poslé takes the genitive — M3's case again — and étovo is the genitive of éhto, said with a v where the g stands.
The plural past: one ending for every gender, which makes my and oní the easy subjects. Imperfective, so it names the activity rather than finishing it.

sentences.trap: rabótali is imperfective and names the activity — we did some working. Nothing was completed and nothing needs to have been, which is why an account can hold both aspects without contradiction.
sentences.sound: sna-CHA-la my ra-BO-ta-li. PO-slye E-ta-va my pash-LI da-MOY. The -ogo of étovo is said -ava.

variations.display: Snachála my rabótali. Potóm my poshlí domóy
variations.script: Сначала мы работали. Потом мы пошли домой
variations.cue: First we worked. Then we went home
variations.changed: the shorter sequencer

variations.display: Poslé étovo ya poshyól v magazín
variations.script: После этого я пошёл в магазин
variations.cue: After that I went to the shop
variations.changed: one person, and a different destination

variations.cue: They worked for two hours
variations.changed: a duration on the same imperfective

mistake.display: Snachála my rabótali. Poslé éhto my poshlí domóy
mistake.script: Сначала мы работали. После это мы пошли домой
mistake.why: poslé takes the genitive: poslé étovo.

sentences.usage: Telling a longer story, where potóm has already been used once.
sentences.mnemonic: poslé takes the genitive, like do.

sentences.cue: In the end I went back home

words.note: The e vanishes when an ending is added — konéts but kontsé — exactly as it does in M2's otéts and ottsá. It is a pattern rather than a quirk.
Perfective, and reflexive in form only — the -sya adds nothing you can translate. Vocabulary, not a system; the -sya rule is L3's.

sentences.trap: domóy has no preposition, exactly as in L1-M5. It is the motion form of dóma, and the pair is the one place in the course where a place word has two shapes and no case behind them.
sentences.sound: v kan-TSE ya vir-NUL-sya da-MOY. The ts is one sound, and the whole line falls to its last syllable.

variations.cue: In the end she went back home
variations.changed: a woman, so -sya becomes -s'

variations.cue: In the end we went home
variations.changed: a plural subject and a simpler verb

variations.cue: I got back at seven o'clock
variations.changed: M6's clock time on the end

mistake.display: V kontsé ya vernúlsya v domóy
mistake.script: В конце я вернулся в домой
mistake.why: domóy takes no preposition: V kontsé ya vernúlsya domóy.

sentences.usage: Closing an account, which Russian does with a marked last step.
sentences.mnemonic: A vanishing e is a pattern, not a quirk.

sentences.display: Ya poteryál klyuch, poéhtomu ya pozvoníl brátu
sentences.script: Я потерял ключ, поэтому я позвонил брату
sentences.cue: I lost my key, so I called my brother
sentences.literal: I lost key, therefore I called to-brother

words.note: M2's brat in the dative, because pozvonít' takes it — the same demand as pomóch' in M1 and pozvonyú in M7. One verb class, one case.

sentences.trap: Both verbs are perfective and the account moves twice. poéhtomu joins them as cause and effect, and neither clause is background to the other.
sentences.sound: ya pa-ti-RYAL klyuch pa-EH-ta-mu ya paz-va-NIL BRA-tu. The dative -u is unstressed and short.

variations.display: Ya poteryála klyuch, poéhtomu ya pozvoníla brátu
variations.script: Я потеряла ключ, поэтому я позвонила брату
variations.cue: I lost my key, so I called my brother
variations.changed: said by a woman — both verbs move

variations.display: Ya poteryál bilét, poéhtomu ya ostálsya dóma
variations.script: Я потерял билет, поэтому я остался дома
variations.cue: I lost my ticket, so I stayed at home
variations.changed: a different problem and a different consequence

variations.cue: I called my brother in the evening
variations.changed: the second half alone, with a time

mistake.display: Ya poteryál klyuch, poéhtomu ya pozvoníl brat
mistake.script: Я потерял ключ, поэтому я позвонил брат
mistake.why: pozvonít' takes the dative: ya pozvoníl brátu.

sentences.usage: The shape of most bad-day stories: a thing went wrong, so I did something.

sentences.display: Snachála býlo khólodno. Potóm my výpili chay. V kontsé my poshlí domóy
sentences.script: Сначала было холодно. Потом мы выпили чай. В конце мы пошли домой
sentences.cue: First it was cold. Then we drank tea. In the end we went home
sentences.literal: At-first was cold. Then we drank-up tea. In end we went home

words.note: skazál's imperfective partner, on its own row as every aspect pair is. It names the activity of talking; skazál names one thing said.

sentences.trap: Three sentences, three steps, and every verb after the first is perfective. The one imperfective is býlo, which is the standing situation the steps happen inside.
sentences.sound: sna-CHA-la BY-la KHO-lad-na. pa-TOM my VY-pi-li chay. v kan-TSE my pash-LI da-MOY. Short sentences and a clear beat on each.

variations.display: Snachála býlo khólodno. Potóm my výpili chay
variations.script: Сначала было холодно. Потом мы выпили чай
variations.cue: First it was cold. Then we drank tea
variations.changed: two steps instead of three

variations.display: Potóm my výpili chay. V kontsé my poshlí domóy
variations.script: Потом мы выпили чай. В конце мы пошли домой
variations.cue: Then we drank tea. In the end we went home
variations.changed: the last two steps

variations.display: On govoríl, no ya ne slýshal
variations.script: Он говорил, но я не слышал
variations.cue: He was talking, but I couldn't hear
variations.changed: two imperfectives — a situation, not an account

mistake.display: Snachála býlo khólodno. Potóm my pili chay. V kontsé my poshlí domóy
mistake.script: Сначала было холодно. Потом мы пили чай. В конце мы пошли домой
mistake.why: A step in an account is perfective: Potóm my výpili chay.

sentences.usage: The whole shape of an account: a situation, some steps, an end.
sentences.mnemonic: The background stands still. The steps move.
